# Review basis

Include this concise record in every substantive review report, even when there are no findings. Fit it into the existing report structure; it does not replace severity, approval or fix-verdict rules.

- **Scope and revision:** What was reviewed, including any narrower fix assignment.
- **Applied resources:** Repository guidance, relevant local/installed skills and unslop profiles actually applied; explain material false-positive boundaries where relevant.
- **Research:** Links to supporting authoritative sources, the claim each establishes and its applicability to this code. Distinguish independently retrieved, dispatcher-supplied and unverified material. State when research was unnecessary or unavailable rather than inventing sources.
- **Proofs:** Focused commands or reproducible checks actually performed, their results and what they resolve. State when no executable proof was needed. Separate existing passing tests from evidence covering the finding.
- **Limits:** Material unavailable capabilities, missing context or unresolved questions and their effect on the assessment. If none were encountered, say so within the actual review scope.

Findings should identify code location, reachable condition, consequence and justified correction. Place unrelated pre-existing observations separately. Do not present a source's general warning as a demonstrated defect, a planned test as a result, or absence of captured tool logs as proof that no tools were used.
